text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A U.S. intelligence report said that Russia held military games in March and April imitating an attack and counterattack with nuclear weapons against NATO, Poland and Lithuania.
- President Algirdas Braauskas plans a three-week holiday after meeting U.S. State Secretary Madeleine Albright on Sunday.
- State-run Agricultural Bank posted a net profit of almost 13 million litas in the first half of 1997.

- The chairman of the privatisation comission said that it will take around three months to draw up a privatisation table for Mazheikiu Nafta refinery and the privatisation process will take much longer.
- The European Commission forecast that according to GDP, Lithuania will beat neigbours Latvia and Estonia.
- Hermis Bank, which had a 14.3 million litas net profit for the first half of the year, has no doubts that it will reach the planned 40.6 million litas profit at the end of 1997.
- Ukio Bank reported a 1.6 million net profit in the first half of 1997 after posting 7.7 million litas of losses in 1996.
- Opponents of privatisation, the Social Democratic Party, collected 120,000 signatures out of 300,000 necessary to arrange a referendum on the privatisation of key companies.
- 143 enterprises out of 312 controlled by the state were operating at a loss in 1996, the state audit department said.
